context: VGLUT1, the canonical glutamatergic gate gene. Confirms a cluster is genuinely excitatory before any layer-specific call is trusted; not layer-informative on its own.

source: Nilssen et al. 2019; Witter et al. 2017
context: Marks the stellate (MEC) / fan+multipolar (LEC) principal cell type in Layer II. This population projects to DG (and likely CA3/CA2) via the perforant path and lacks monosynaptic connections to other principal cells. In your data this is the population Excit.L2_5.2 registers to (Sestan EC.L2.RELN.BMPR1B), not Excit.L2.

Upper-layer marker; co-occurs with RELN/ADARB2 in the Sestan atlas label for Excit.L2_5.2 (EC.L3.PCP4.ADARB2). Useful to confirm the RELN-lineage upper-layer population distinct from the CALB1+ pyramidal type.
Component of the Sestan reference label for Excit.L2_5.2 (EC.L3.PCP4.ADARB2), surfaced via your spatial registration data. Secondary confirmatory marker alongside RELN/PCP4.
Component of the Sestan reference label for Excit.L2_5.2 (EC.L2.RELN.BMPR1B), surfaced via your spatial registration data. Secondary confirmatory marker for the RELN-lineage L2 population.

source: Nilssen et al. 2019; Witter et al. 2017
context: Marks the pyramidal principal cell type in Layer II (both MEC/LEC). Projects broadly to CA1, other EC targets, and commissurally; ~50% also make local excitatory connections within EC. Confirmed as the #4 MeanRatio gene for Excit.L2 in your data, consistent with Sestan label EC.L2.CUX2.CALB1.
Canonical L2/3 upper-layer marker; forms part of the Sestan label for Excit.L2 (EC.L2.CUX2.CALB1). Good general upper-layer confirmatory marker alongside CALB1.
Upper-layer marker gene, not yet assigned to the RELN vs. CALB1 subtype split specifically. Useful as a general upper-layer (L2/3) confirmatory marker.
Upper-layer marker gene. General L2/3 confirmatory marker, not subtype-resolved.
Upper-layer marker gene. General L2/3 confirmatory marker, not subtype-resolved.

source: Franjic et al. 2022; Leng et al. 2021
context: Mid-to-deep layer marker and the specific marker Leng et al. 2021 identified for the selectively vulnerable excitatory population in caudal EC (validated against neurofibrillary tangle burden). Confirmed as the #3 MeanRatio gene for Excit.L5.1 (Sestan EC.L5.RORB.TLL1). Leading candidate marker for a Layer Va-like (output-projecting) identity.
Component of the Sestan reference label for Excit.L5.1 (EC.L5.RORB.TLL1). Secondary confirmatory marker alongside RORB.

Rodent Layer Va marker — Va cells are the major output-projecting sublayer, sending axons to diverse cortical/subcortical targets. Not yet checked in your data; testing ETV1 in Excit.L5.1 vs. Excit.L5.2 would help confirm or refute L5.1=Va, L5.2=Vb.

Human gene symbol for Ctip2, the rodent Layer Vb marker. Vb neurons project back to Va and to Layers II/III — the deep-to-superficial feedback loop. Appears as a component of the Sestan label for Excit.L5.2 (EC.L2.RELN.BCL11B), which may explain why L5.2 clusters transcriptomically near the L2/RELN lineage despite its anatomical Layer V position.
Mid-to-deep layer marker, shared across several deep Excit clusters rather than resolving a single sublayer. General deep-layer confirmatory marker.
Mid-to-deep layer marker. General deep-layer confirmatory marker, not sublayer-resolved.

General deep-layer marker, shared across the Sestan labels for Excit.L5_6_NP, Excit.L6_CT, and Excit.L6b. Confirms deep/infragranular identity broadly but does not by itself distinguish NP vs. CT vs. L6b.

Confirmed as the #4 MeanRatio gene for Excit.L5_6_NP in your data (Sestan EC.L56.TLE4.NXPH2). Commonly used to mark 'near-projecting' deep-layer excitatory subtypes in general cortical literature, though that cross-species convention wasn't independently re-verified here — the atlas registration is the solid evidence.

source: General cortical NP literature (untested in EC)
context: Paralog marker often paired with NXPH2 for the near-projecting (NP) subtype in general cortical atlases. Not yet checked in your data or confirmed EC-specific — included as a cross-validation candidate for the Excit.L5_6_NP call, not a confirmed finding.
Confirmed as the #5 MeanRatio gene for Excit.L6_CT in your data (Sestan EC.L6.TLE4.SULF1). Currently the strongest direct evidence for this cluster's identity.

source: General neocortical CT literature (untested in EC)
context: Classic neocortical corticothalamic (CT) marker. Did NOT appear in either top-10 marker list for Excit.L6_CT, and Nilssen 2019 notes detailed EC Layer VI connectional data is largely lacking. Recommend an explicit expression check — this is a hypothesis to test, not a confirmed EC marker.

source: General neocortical CT literature (untested in EC)
context: Classic neocortical CT marker, usually paired with FOXP2. Not yet checked in your data — same purpose as FOXP2, would strengthen the L6_CT call if positive.
Confirmed as the #4 enrichment gene for Excit.L6b. Classic subplate/Layer 6b marker in both mouse and human cortex. Your strongest and best-supported deep-layer call.

Also known as CTGF. Paired subplate marker with CPLX3 in the same reference. Appears as a component of the Sestan label for Excit.L6b (EC.L6b.TLE4.CCN2) — you've independently recovered both halves of this classic marker pair from two different statistics.
